newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Strikes, marches, bombs shake Honduras.
newsitem.headline: Strikes, marches, bombs shake Honduras.

text.p: Honduras on Wednesday was shaken by a hospital workers' strike and army troops patrolled main cities after five U.S. food outlets were damaged by explosions overnight.

Five explosive devices were set off late on Tuesday in the northern city of San Pedro Sula outside outlets of Burger King, Pizza Hut, McDonalds, Wendy's and Friday's, said Col. Luis Velazquez, head of an army base near the city.
The blasts caused damage to the restaurants but no casualties, police said. No group claimed responsibility. No details were available on the damages.
Some 14,000 public health workers virtually paralysed hospitals, launching an indefinite strike against what they said was an insuffient government pay offer.

"We have reports that all hospitals and health centres have attended our call. We will only attend those already hospitalized and emergency cases," Faustino Martinez, head of the health workers' union, told Reuters.

The start of the hospital strike coincided with scheduled marches by thousands of members of the country's three main labour confederations, demanding price stability for basic goods and cuts in costs of transportation and fuel.

The country's president, Carlos Roberto Reina, 70, has faced growing unrest from the country's 70,000 public sector workers, who argued that government pay offers this year fell short of living wages.
Honduras' Security Council, made up of military chiefs and cabinet members, met on Tuesday to discuss the crisis, and affirmed their full support for Reina, ministers said.
On Wednesday, Reina branded the five bombings an assault on democracy.
